title: Reading a downloaded workflow before you run it

questions.q: Opening a workflow JSON in a text editor is:
options: Safe in itself: it is data, and you are only reading
Dangerous, because JSON can run code
Only safe in ComfyUI
Only safe on a CPU
questions.answer: Safe in itself: it is data, and you are only reading
questions.why: JSON is data. The risks come from what it leads you to install, download or send.

questions.q: A graph uses a node type your server doesn't have. What is the real risk?
options: Installing the pack it needs runs that pack's code on your machine
Queueing it runs code from the file
The missing node will download itself
There is none
questions.answer: Installing the pack it needs runs that pack's code on your machine
questions.why: Queueing just gives missing_node_type. ComfyUI imports packs when it starts, so the install is the step that needs care.

questions.q: A graph uses a partner API node with your prompt in it. What happens if you queue it with an account signed in?
options: The prompt goes to an outside service, and it can spend credits
Nothing leaves your machine
It runs on your GPU
It is refused by validation
questions.answer: The prompt goes to an outside service, and it can spend credits
questions.why: That's the job of these nodes. ComfyUI's own help text calls them the paid API nodes.

questions.q: You scanned the canvas and every node looks familiar. What can still be hidden?
options: Nodes inside a subgraph, which shows as one box
Nothing, the canvas shows every node
Only the seed
Only the file names
questions.answer: Nodes inside a subgraph, which shows as one box
questions.why: definitions.subgraphs holds whole inner graphs. In the lab one third-party node appears only there.

questions.q: A note in a workflow says to paste a command into your terminal to fix an error. What do you do?
options: Read what the command does and find out where it came from, and don't paste it blind
Paste it: notes are checked by ComfyUI
Paste it: it only runs inside ComfyUI
Ignore all notes in all workflows
questions.answer: Read what the command does and find out where it came from, and don't paste it blind
questions.why: A note is plain text from the author. It runs nothing by itself, and you would be the one to run it.
